articles.title: Letter: The Street Tree Planting on Warren Court Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Warren Court for 4 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. has made.
Please keep the street tree planting in the budget. Many of us on Warren Court use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Julia Rooney, Canal Park

articles.title: Council Tables Street Tree Planting Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 21 residents spoke at Monday’s session.
body: Residents of Mill Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Hal Gilroy, 82, Longtime Crossing Guard
articles.deck: Friends remember Hal Gilroy for the many years of service to Tannery Flats.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

Born in Tannery Flats in the years after the war, Hal Gilroy spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Tannery Flats.
Hal Gilroy died in April at home on Lilac Street, at the age of 82. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

articles.title: Then & Now: the Hickory Ridge Rec Center, 1999 and 2026
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1999 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Bramble Terrace from the corner of Warren Court. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.
